who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane N7 of the no-C-library change
where: pins/clang.json (shelf_programs), pins/rust.txt; crates/blaze-sys/src/macos_block.rs, macos.rs ffi, seatbelt.rs, posix/proc/status.rs
what: Writing scripts/src/bin/sys_imports.rs (nm -u over a built blaze-sys rlib): the only pinned llvm-nm is the macOS arm64 shelf's (clang.json: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu's shelf names nothing) and the Rust pin has no llvm-tools component, so a Linux gate host has no pinned nm to run, and the Mac needs the shelf's path, which nothing prints. Reading blaze-sys for the macOS list also met: crates/blaze-sys/src/macos_block.rs is declared by no `mod` (it reads like compiled code and is not), and `clonefile` and `__error` are each declared twice (macos.rs's ffi and posix/proc/status.rs; macos.rs's ffi and seatbelt.rs), against rule 30.
cost: about twenty minutes of grepping for an nm and checking which files are compiled
cause: the shelf pins only what native build scripts start; the orphan file and the second declarations came from parallel lanes
whys: no check asks for a binary-level tool on every host; nothing refuses a .rs file under src/ that no module declares
class: a tool a gate needs that is pinned on one host only; a source file that is not compiled
prevention: pin llvm-nm for every host (the shelf's row for Linux hosts, or llvm-tools in pins/rust.txt), and a docs-style check that every .rs under a crate's src/ is reached by a `mod` or `#[path]`
annoyance: the sys_imports input takes `nm` as a path because no pinned one exists everywhere
workaround: the coordinator passes the shelf's <shelf>/bin/llvm-nm on the Mac, or any llvm-nm on Linux (llvm-nm reads ELF and Mach-O on any host)
